clue.text: Local over by naturism centre curious, plainly

parts.note: a local is a pub, the nearest inn

indicators.note: something curious is odd or strange, so the preceding words are put into an odd new order

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
both words taken whole as raw letters

explanation.surface: A pub-goer's frank verdict on some odd goings-on at the local nudist colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' looks like an instruction to take middle letters of naturism, but both words are the full anagram fodder. A local is British slang for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in no uncertain terms means stating it clearly and bluntly, which is to speak plainly.

clue.text: 'Enemies of Trump' in retreat after revolution? Not your concern

indicators.note: the quoted enemies are placed inside the retreat that follows
a revolution turns something round, so the retreat is written backwards

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
Donald Trump notoriously described his political enemies as vermin

explanation.surface: A headline about Trump's opponents backing off after an uprising, shrugged off as none of your business.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks point to Trump's own word for his enemies; the retreat is reversed and then wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Never mind' is an idiom telling someone a matter need not worry them, i.e. it is not their concern.

clue.text: Turn up on Sabbath to see Giants

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go
on in the sense of concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: Sabbath is shortened to its usual one-letter abbreviation, its initial

parts.note: S abbreviates Sabbath

explanation.surface: Showing up on a Sunday to watch the Giants play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as one phrasal verb, but turn is the word and up tells you to flip it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore, so they are an example of giants.

clue.text: Oz actor's prepared for punch

parts.note: Jimmy Nail played the character Oz in the TV comedy-drama Auf Wiedersehen, Pet; the 's means 'is'
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: An Australian actor is ready to throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz looks like Australia, but it is a character name: Jimmy Nail played Oz, a Geordie bricklayer, in the British series Auf Wiedersehen, Pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail set is a small metal punch used to drive nail heads below a wood surface.

clue.text: After negotiation, agreed about navy's defensive position

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the navy
a negotiated settlement is reworked from the original, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: Following talks, the parties settle on what the navy's defensive stance should be.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take the guard stance, a defensive position ready for attack.

clue.text: Go for tramp: 'Be on your way!'

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, set off on a long walk
second meaning: a rude dismissal telling someone to leave

explanation.walkthrough: Tramp reads like a vagrant being told to move along, but it is the noun for a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to go on a long walk and, as a slang command, to clear off.

clue.text: Idealised representation of current Chairman taking in government

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so the chairman holds the next piece

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese leader
G abbreviates government

explanation.surface: An idealised portrait of the present chairman bringing in a new administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current Chairman' reads as the one now in office, but current is the electrical symbol and Chairman is Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychoanalysis an imago is an unconscious idealised mental image of a person, such as a parent.

clue.text: Only biter gets teeth kicked in outside: exactly what's required

parts.note: only and just both mean merely

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled teeth wrap round the biter
teeth that are kicked in are knocked out of place, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
a tick is a bloodsucking parasite that bites

explanation.surface: A violent bar scene: the only one who bit someone gets his teeth kicked in outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The biter is not a person but a parasite; the first block comes first, then the rearranged teeth enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Just the ticket' is an idiom for something that is precisely what is needed.

clue.text: Policeman grabbing one thug's head at fair is in a good place

indicators.note: grabbing means holding on to, so the policeman encloses what follows

parts.note: Sting was the singer of the band The Police
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of thug
fair and pretty both mean good-looking

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a thug at the fun fair and is well pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The policeman is a member of The Police, the rock band, not a constable; the fair is an adjective, not a fun fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting pretty is an idiom for being in a comfortable, advantageous situation.

clue.text: Navy ruing new uniform

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the words before are put into a fresh order

parts.note: both words taken whole as raw letters

explanation.surface: The navy regrets introducing a new uniform for its sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform reads as sailors' clothing, but it is the adjective meaning the same throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means consistent and unchanging, a synonym of unvarying.

clue.text: Reportedly starter's in shade

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the solver listens for a sound match

parts.note: a car key is what starts a car's engine

explanation.surface: Word is the first course is served in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter suggests a first course, but here it is what you start a car with; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish-yellow colour, so it is one shade among many.

clue.text: See 1
Talk about one day inside as stretch!

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so these pieces go into the talk

parts.note: to spout is to talk at length
re means about or concerning
AD, anno Domini, marks a year of our Lord, read here as a single day

explanation.surface: A prisoner talks about doing a day inside as a stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' and 'stretch' both suggest prison time, but stretch is an imperative: spread out!
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch is to extend the limbs or body, and 'Spread out!' is the same command.

clue.text: Say, Bob Hope's first appearance at nick

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: first letter of Hope
an air is a manner or appearance
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: Bob Hope makes his first appearance at the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Hope looks like one name, but Bob is the definition, flagged by 'Say' as an example; nick is also British slang for a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head, an example of a haircut.

clue.text: Against type one initially agreed they pool their resources

parts.note: con as in pros and cons, the case against
a type is a kind or sort
Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially means taking only the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: first letter of agreed

explanation.surface: Contrary types who nonetheless agreed to share their funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are associations of companies that combine their money and assets for a joint venture.

clue.text: Jan 6 events no small issue

indicators.note: no small means the letter standing for small is taken away

parts.note: the storming of the US Capitol on 6 January 2021 was widely called sedition

explanation.surface: The January 6th riot was no minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one edition of it.

clue.text: Protecting all but American showing disrespect

indicators.note: all but means everything except, so the letter for American is removed

parts.note: insulating means shielding or protecting

explanation.surface: Shielding everyone except the American comes across as rude.
explanation.walkthrough: A is the usual abbreviation for American.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting words are rude and offensive, the way of showing disrespect to someone.

clue.text: Inspector Troy back in force beginning to show intelligence

indicators.note: back means the inspector and Troy's initial are read in the opposite order

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, used here and for Troy

parts.note: first letter of Troy
taken as written
g is the physics symbol for gravitational force
first letter of show

explanation.surface: Detective Inspector Troy rejoins the force and starts to show some intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy looks like a fictional detective's surname, but only its initial is wanted; force is a physics symbol, not the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of news or information received is the same as tidings.

clue.text: Don't change it round! Composer in the end kept faster pieces of music

indicators.note: kept means held, so the proofreader's instruction holds the letter

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning leave it as it was

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of composer

parts.note: last letter of composer

indicators.note: turned round means written in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer insists his music be left alone, yet in the end keeps faster passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't change it' reads as one instruction, but it splits: the first two words are the proofreading term, and it is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti, plural of stretto, are passages played at a quickened tempo, typically near a piece's close.

clue.text: Starts talking freely in drink with old writer

parts.note: O abbreviates old
a pen is a writing instrument
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: An old author becomes talkative once he has had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is placed last, after the old writer, though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is an idiom for beginning to speak candidly about one's feelings.

clue.text: Coming back, piece of trifle's enough for me

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so read right to left
a piece of something is a portion of it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: On the second helping, one piece of trifle is plenty for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Oneself is the reflexive pronoun for an indefinite person, used in place of myself, or me.

clue.text: Lobby politician — Hunt?

parts.note: a Con is a Conservative politician
to course is to hunt hares with dogs; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: Lobby the politician Jeremy Hunt, who might be a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Lobby looks like a verb for pressuring a politician, and Hunt like Jeremy Hunt, the Conservative minister; both are misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a large open hall in a station or airport, a kind of lobby.

clue.text: New teacher not good about Australia: 'It's a tiny country'

indicators.note: about means going round, so the teacher surrounds Australia
not good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: N abbreviates new
a guru is a spiritual teacher
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: A new teacher, poor on Australian geography, insists it is a tiny country.
explanation.walkthrough: The teacher goes round A to give GAURU, and then G for good is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru, a Pacific island nation, is one of the smallest countries in the world by area.

clue.text: Comfort lecturer in bar

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: bar and save both mean except
L abbreviates lecturer

explanation.surface: Consoling a lecturer down at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar suggests a pub but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: To salve is to soothe or ease someone's feelings, which is to comfort them.

clue.text: Mostly arrest snoopers

indicators.note: mostly means almost all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: stasis is a stoppage or arrest of movement

explanation.surface: Secret police spend most of their time arresting people.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrest suggests police detaining someone but means a halt, as in cardiac arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was the East German secret police, notorious for spying on citizens.

clue.text: Boil over with umpire finally at game point

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of umpire

parts.note: last letter of umpire
RU is rugby union
PT abbreviates point

explanation.surface: Tempers flare against the umpire at match point.
explanation.walkthrough: Game point sounds like tennis, but the words split into a sport's initials and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out violently, as a pot or a temper boils over.

clue.text: Possibly shrink shirt egghead Pat's worn

indicators.note: worn suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the head of egg is its first letter
taken as written; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: Pat the intellectual has worn the shirt so much it may well shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink reads as a verb about laundry, but it is slang for a psychiatrist; egghead is one word split into egg plus head.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, and a therapist is possibly one, hence the qualifier.

clue.text: Unfit! Clearing out extremists in party

indicators.note: out suggests something disordered or wrong, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: both words taken whole as raw letters

explanation.surface: A party purge: the unfit are cleared out as extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearing out' reads as one phrasal verb, but clearing is fodder and out alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunatic fringe is the wild minority within a political movement holding extreme views.
